title: Microsoft Purview Information Protection: File Labeler and File Viewer for macOS
summary: Hold: the licensing model is reported as unpublished even though Microsoft's billing guidance explicitly covers protections on macOS endpoints under per-user licensing. The briefing also overstates label policies as deciding who may lower or remove a label; the sources describe justification settings and separate protection permissions instead.

claims.claim: The client described by the cited Learn client page runs on Windows only.
claims.quote: This client runs on Windows only and replaces the Azure Information Protection (AIP) unified labeling client.

claims.claim: The Windows File Labeler applies sensitivity labels and encryption using File Explorer.
claims.quote: Used to apply sensitivity labels and encryption using File Explorer.

claims.quote: Used to view files that are encrypted.

claims.claim: Advanced label-based protection is an endpoint DLP setting for labeling and encrypting non-Office, non-PDF files with the client.
claims.quote: This setting enhances productivity for users that label and encrypt file types other than those for Office and PDF by using the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client.

claims.claim: On Windows, Advanced label-based protection lets these files retain their original extension while on the device.
claims.quote: When a user selects a sensitivity label that applies encryption, the file name extension now doesn't change.

claims.claim: Without that setting, Windows client encryption changes these files' extensions.
claims.quote: The encrypted file changes its file name extension and becomes read-only, and can no longer be opened by apps that support the original file name extension.

claims.claim: Without that setting, these encrypted files open in the Information Protection Viewer.
claims.quote: Instead, the file opens in the Microsoft Purview Information Protection viewer.

claims.claim: Access to protected content depends on the permissions in its encryption.
claims.quote: Control access to content by using encryption for emails, meeting invites, and documents to prevent unauthorized people from accessing this data.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels to sources for the general encryption-based access-control statement; retain the notice as the source for existing policies continuing on macOS.

claims.claim: Label policy settings decide who may lower or remove a label.
claims.quote: Searched: sensitivity label policy remove downgrade labels justification permissions File Labeler. Read create-sensitivity-labels, sensitivity-labels and Label and protect files in File Explorer in Windows; found justification settings and separate protection-removal rights.
claims.fix: Replace 'Whether a user may do so follows the label policy, so review the policy settings that decide who can lower or remove a label before Mac users get the client.' with 'Microsoft's notice says existing sensitivity labeling policies continue to apply; test label changes and removal with representative Mac users before wider deployment.'

claims.claim: Label publishing policies select which users and groups receive sensitivity labels and policy settings.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal route Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label opens label policy creation.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. On the Label policies page, select Publish label to start the Create policy configuration.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AddLabels <label names> adds sensitivity labels to an identified policy.
claims.quote: The AddLabels parameter specifies the sensitivity labels that you want to add to the policy. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the label. For example: Name

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy functions only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Using Set-LabelPolicy requires assigned permissions documented for the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions. For more information, see Permissions in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.

claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'per-user'.
